description: The short Heritage escape spelling `op`, EXECUTED at the top level, carries the same CANONICAL `params.keyword` `"return"` as `output` and as Core `return` (issue #741) — `code`, `params`, `stage` and `severity` byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/execution/procedure-return-outside-proc`, and to the sibling `heritage/execution/heritage-output-canonical-keyword-executed-outside-proc`. Both Heritage spellings are fixtured because a param that varies with the spelling varies per spelling: `op` is a separate surface word reaching the same `params`, and asserting only `output` would leave the value `op` produces unpinned. `source_span` covers the whole `op 5` statement (4 columns against the 8 of `output 5`), so a shorter spelling still spans what the learner wrote — canonicalizing the param did not canonicalize the span. The prose still says `op`, which the localization boundary `spec/error-model.md:255-260` permits. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
